title: Wisdom's children (Luke 7:18–35)
hookLine: John had doubts in prison; Jesus answers with what's happening
carry: go and tell what you've seen

lines: ART THOU HE THAT SHOULD COME?
cards: John the Baptist is locked up. Luke told us earlier that Herod shut him in prison for criticizing the ruler's marriage. The man who lived in open desert air now sits in a cell.
His followers bring him news: healings, crowds, a widow's son raised. News like that might encourage him.
Instead, John sends two of his disciples to Jesus with a question that sounds like doubt: "Art thou he that should come? or look we for another?"
This is the man who baptized Jesus, who said he wasn't worthy to untie his sandals. Even John, it seems, can wonder in the dark.

teach.b: Jesus doesn't scold John for asking, and doesn't even answer yes.

Luke says that in that same hour he healed many, then told the messengers: "Go your way, and tell John what things ye have seen and heard; how that the blind see, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, to the poor the gospel is preached."
Not an argument: a report. The list echoes the scroll of Isaiah that Jesus read in Nazareth, sight to the blind, good news to the poor, and lets John draw the line himself.

teach.h: BLESSED IS HE NOT OFFENDED IN ME.
teach.b: Then a gentle line: "And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me." Behind offended is the Greek skandalizo, to trip up; its noun, skandalon, is a snare or stumbling block.
Blessed is anyone who doesn't trip over a Messiah different from what they expected.
As soon as the messengers leave, Jesus praises John: "Among those that are born of women there is not a greater prophet than John the Baptist." The question hasn't lowered him.

teach.h: WE PIPED AND YE DID NOT DANCE.
teach.b: Then a picture of children in the marketplace, complaining: we played the flute and you didn't dance; we sang a sad song and you didn't cry. John came fasting, and some said he had a devil.
Jesus came eating and drinking, and some called him a glutton. Nothing satisfies the critics.

teach.h: WISDOM IS JUSTIFIED OF ALL HER CHILDREN.
teach.b: "But wisdom is justified of all her children." Wisdom is proved right by what she produces.

how: Some churches read Matthew's telling of John's question from prison during Advent, and some Christians take comfort that even John the Baptist sent his doubt to Jesus as a question.

o: wise teachers who came before the prophets
the lives that prove wisdom right
children taught proverbs from an early age

games.q: what's inside Luke 7:18–35 — tap the pairs.
p: art thou he that should come?
tell John what ye have seen and heard
we piped, and ye have not danced

s: he answered with what was happening, then praised John to the crowd.
Jesus' answer echoes the Isaiah scroll he read in Nazareth
sight to the blind, good news to the poor.
it's from skandalon: a snare, something to stumble over.

games.q: John sends messengers asking: are you the one, or should we look for someone else? how do you answer?
o: yes, of course. tell him to stop doubting.
go and tell John what you've seen and heard.
say nothing; he should already know.
games.why: Jesus answers with evidence, the blind seeing and the poor hearing good news, and lets John decide. then he tells the crowd no prophet is greater than John.

practice: Some questions are hard to say out loud, about faith, a relationship, a path already chosen; if you have one, name it plainly in a sentence, the way John did, without answering it.

Then, instead of an argument, think about what you've actually seen and heard lately that speaks to it, either way. If you pray, you can ask your question to God plainly; if you don't, simply hold it with honesty.

wordCard.voice: Wisdom's children. John asks from prison whether Jesus is the one, and Jesus answers with what's happening, and says wisdom is proved right by her children.

orig.note: Greek: a snare, a trap's trigger, a stumbling block. behind "offended" in Luke 7:23.

carryVoice: Your line: go and tell what you've seen. Asking didn't make John any smaller. See you tomorrow.
